summary: A line chart of one series with a computed y axis, for any measurement that moves over time and may have a reference value: a price, a balance, heart rate, temperature. Line with a fading area, axis labels on round ticks, an optional baseline with one colour above and another below, high and low marks, x labels, the latest value in a tag. Use it rather than LineChart when the axis must follow data the host replaces; LineChart when you write the labels yourself or plot several series. Fills its box and drops axes and marks when small.

values.doc: A float array, "@name" of resources.floatArrays, export it so the host can replace it. Oldest first; any length of 1 or more; any range, negative too

baseline.doc: A reference value such as previous close: a dashed line with its value at the axis, the line and area green above and red below. The y range always includes it. Without it, the whole line takes the colour of last against first

points.doc: How many samples the full period will have (390 for a US trading day in minutes): a day still in progress stops short, with a vertical marker at now and the rest empty, instead of stretching. Default: the array's length

minRange.doc: The y axis spans at least this fraction of the price (0.01 is 1%), so a 0.1% wobble does not fill the chart and read as a crash. 0 scales to min and max

decimals.doc: Decimals of the latest price, the baseline and the marks, for values under 1000; more are used if the ticks are finer (a price of 0.0042). 0 for whole units such as kWh or bpm. Above 1000, the axis switches to K, M, B, T

color.doc: Give it when up and down don't mean good and bad (heart rate, energy, visits): one colour for line, area and tag, no direction

xLabels.doc: Labels under the chart, spread evenly from left to right: ["10am", "12pm", "2pm", "4pm"]. Only first and last are kept when narrow

marks.doc: Dot and value at the highest and lowest points (not when the latest price is that point, its tag says it)

area.doc: The fading wash under the line, a smooth gradient (never in mono)

yAxis.doc: Tick labels and the latest-price tag on the right; dropped by itself under 200 dp wide

surface.doc: The colour behind the chart: the halo that keeps the high and low labels clear of grid lines, and the colour the area fades into. Set it if the chart is not on @colors.surface

fill.doc: Fill the space the caller gives it, so the widget decides the size

label.doc: What the chart is, spoken before the latest, high and low

pitfalls: Use this rather than LineChart for a single series judged against a reference or read off an axis (a price, a balance, heart rate): LineChart's axis labels are fixed text you write, these are computed from the data, on round steps (1, 2, 5 × 10ⁿ), and move when the host replaces the array. Finance is only its default: without color, green means up and red down, so pass color for anything else

Which chart: PriceChart for a hero chart of one series with an axis; TrendSparkline for a word-sized trend in a row; LineChart for time-of-day curves with function mode or labels you choose; BarChart for separate quantities
The line is straight segments through the samples, not a spline: a spline invents highs and lows between prices. High and low are the samples' own; pass the session's real high and low in your stats

Set a height through fill and a sized parent: with fill in a column, give the parent a verticalWeight or an exact height. Under 200 dp wide the y axis and marks go, under 110 dp tall the x labels go, so a 2x2 widget keeps line, area, baseline and dot

Every number on the axis is a text built at run time (printed with six decimals and cut), about 6.5 KB a chart, 7.5 KB with a baseline. It is meant for the one hero chart of a screen; rows take TrendSparkline
Mono: no area and no direction colours. With a baseline the line is white above and grey below; the tag is a filled face
A float holds about 7 digits: prices above 99,999.99 lose cents on the axis
The area fades to `surface` under an alpha, not to transparent, so it looks the same in every player: on another background, pass that colour as surface or the bottom edge of the wash shows faintly
